rules.jsxText: JSX text nodes; whitespace runs (space, tab, newline) collapsed, trimmed; entities decoded (raw keeps the undecoded form when it differs).
rules.attr: JSX attribute values for: title, aria-label, placeholder, alt, aria-description, aria-roledescription, label, aria-valuetext, aria-placeholder, unit, heading, caption, hint, subtitle, emptyText, and any *Label prop; expression values contribute every string they can render (both ?: arms, || ?? && sides).
rules.jsxChild: context "jsxChild": string/template rendered as a JSX child through an expression ({cond ? "A" : "B"}).
rules.imperative: source "imperative": strings assigned to textContent/innerText/title/placeholder/ariaLabel or passed to canvas fillText.
rules.listed: source "listed": every remaining literal/template in frontend/src/features/layer-picker/LayerDropdown.tsx, frontend/src/components/Fleet/roverMeta.ts, frontend/src/components/Fleet/FleetSelectionView.tsx, frontend/src/features/registry.ts, frontend/src/SplashScreen.tsx, frontend/src/LandingPage.tsx, frontend/src/components/TopBar/TopBar.tsx, frontend/src/App.tsx, frontend/src/i18n/reportCopy.ts, frontend/src/features/assistant/, frontend/src/features/mission-report/ (registry.ts: RAIL_TABS labels only), after exclusions.
rules.heuristic: source "heuristic": remaining literals in other frontend/src/features/** files that contain a letter and either whitespace or a leading capital.
rules.template: kind "template": static parts kept, each ${...} written as {…}; expressions lists the substituted source text.
rules.uncertain: kind "uncertain": a literal from a listed file rejected by a filter (reason says which); excluded from the coverage set.
rules.excluded: never recorded: import specifiers, type positions, property names, non-visible JSX attributes (className, style, key, data-*, ...), console.* arguments.
rules.lang: reportCopy.ts takes language from its enclosing en/tr key or lang === "tr" ternary; elsewhere tr when Turkish letters or common Turkish words appear, mixed when English function words appear as well.

Under the benchmark’s own motion model, LunaPath reproduces the paper’s shortest-path lengths exactly (
MoonPlanBench maps are slope/roughness-thresholded occupancy grids only — no shadow,
thermal, slip, roughness or Earth-visibility layer, and no DEM released — at 320 m to
7,680 m per cell. LunaPath’s multi-criteria cost is a single value on them and its
planner reduces to a shortest-path search with its own safety rules. Success here
measures connectivity under a motion model, not rover route planning. The benchmark’s
reference planners allow diagonal moves between two occupied cells; LunaPath refuses
them. Every paper figure is a quotation from arXiv 2512.21438v1, not our measurement.

How hard the solver works to avoid steep ground. Raise it and the route detours around inclines and crater rims; lower it and it takes the shorter, steeper line.
What battery drain costs the route. Raise it to favour flatter, shorter traverses that arrive with charge to spare; lower it when arrival time matters more than the power budget.
How strongly the route avoids permanently shadowed ground. Raise it to keep the rover in sunlight for power and warmth; lower it when the science target sits inside a cold trap.
How strongly the route avoids extreme cold. Raise it to keep the rover inside its survival temperature band; lower it to accept colder ground for a shorter path.

How strongly the route avoids broken ground, measured by NASA’s LOLA laser altimetry. Raise it to buy smoother driving with energy and time; lower it to take the direct line over rougher terrain. Only shown where the measured roughness layer is loaded.
